Size = crash volume · Click markers for details
Not on the map: 3,392 of 331,034 crashes (1.0%) have no usable coordinates in the Chicago Open Data records. They are counted in every total and chart on this page.
Privacy: This page has no backend, no analytics, and no cookies, and nothing you type is stored by crashmaps. Loading it fetches fonts from Google Fonts, scripts from cdnjs (Cloudflare) and map tiles from CARTO, and each of those services sees your IP address. An address you search is sent to OpenStreetMap Nominatim, and commute start and end points are sent to the public OSRM routing server. Those requests are subject to each service’s privacy policy.

14 — Methodology

How I Built This

Data pipeline: Crash records queried from Chicago’s Socrata API (dataset 85ca-t3if), paginated at 50,000 records per call. 108,796 records for 2025. Coordinates are native WGS84.
Region assignment: Chicago is divided into 10 geographic regions (Loop, North Side, South Side, etc.) using lat/lon bounding boxes. Crashes outside defined boundaries are excluded.
Behavioral flags: Hit-and-run from hit_and_run_i field (Y/N). Impairment from "UNDER THE INFLUENCE OF ALCOHOL/DRUGS" contributing cause. Speed from "FAILING TO REDUCE SPEED TO AVOID CRASH." Pedestrian/cyclist from first_crash_type field.
Hotspots: A hotspot is every crash within roughly a 200-metre area. All 65 hotspots on this page come from records that give a street with no cross street. Those are grouped by 200-metre square and labelled “[street] near [nearest cross street]”, with the cross street taken from OpenStreetMap. The count covers every crash in the square, including crashes on the other streets inside it. Squares next to each other are listed separately.

Data: Chicago Data Portal · Vision Zero · IDOT
Unofficial. Built from public agency records, which the agencies do not guarantee to be complete or accurate; not for legal use. Intersection names and route lines © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL).
